gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Romania produces in a year, at current prices, on a rolling four-quarter basis.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each historical point using that year's own average leu rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF, annual resolution, coarser than the monthly or daily matching on most other countries here, since no free monthly or daily US dollar series exists for the leu).
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to Romania's real (chained-volume, inflation-adjusted) GDP series (Eurostat namq_10_gdp, CLV20_MNAC). This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.source: Eurostat namq_10_gdp (CP_MNAC) · current prices, lei, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarterly, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum, from 2000.

gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, shown in chained-volume terms, the same production, valued at constant prices, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.dollar: Same matching as GDP (current prices): each point converted at its own year's average leu rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF).
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.
gdp_real.source: Eurostat namq_10_gdp (CLV20_MNAC) · chain-linked volumes, 2020 reference year, lei, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarterly, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum, from 2000.

gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real (inflation-adjusted) terms. The National Institute of Statistics's first estimate is often revised; this shows the latest published figure.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying lei to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate as published, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.source: Derived from Eurostat namq_10_gdp (CLV20_MNAC) · real GDP, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarter-on-quarter, from 2000.

cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago, on the EU's harmonised index (HICP), shown for comparison with other EU countries. The National Institute of Statistics's headline is the national CPI, shown beside it, which the National Bank of Romania targets at 2.5% (plus or minus one point). The two differ more than in most EU countries because their weights differ.
cpi.source: FRED series CP0000ROM086NEST · HICP, all items, year on year, from January 2002.

cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the month, on the EU's harmonised measure. A monthly change is not the annual rate divided by twelve: it is the change on the month before, so it moves with one-off price changes that the annual rate smooths out.
cpi_mom.source: Derived from FRED series CP0000ROM086NEST (Eurostat) · HICP, all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted, from January 2002.

cpi_national.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago, on the National Institute of Statistics's national CPI, the headline figure and the measure the National Bank of Romania targets at 2.5% (plus or minus one point).
cpi_national.source: IMF consumer price index dataset (INS national CPI) · CPI, national definition, all items, year on year, as published by the National Institute of Statistics, from January 2002. The IMF publishes it about a month after INS, so the latest month here can be one behind INS's release.

policy_rate.description: The monetary policy rate, the National Bank of Romania's main policy rate. Shown from August 2005, when the NBR adopted inflation targeting.
policy_rate.source: BIS central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL, M.RO, extended with the daily series D.RO) · NBR monetary policy rate, end of month, from August 2005; the current month shows the latest rate.

bond_yield_10y.description: The yield on 10-year Romanian government bonds, a market gauge of inflation and interest-rate expectations. This is not the NBR's own policy rate.
bond_yield_10y.source: ECB long-term interest rate for convergence purposes (IRS, M.RO.L.L40.CI.0000.RON.N.Z) · 10-year government bond yield, monthly average, from 2001.

unemployment.description: The share of people aged 15 to 74 in the labour force who want a job and are actively looking, but can't find one.
unemployment.source: Eurostat une_rt_m · unemployment rate, ILO definition, ages 15 to 74, seasonally adjusted, monthly, from January 2009.

exports.description: The value of goods Romania sells to the rest of the world each month, in lei.
exports.dollar: Each point is converted at its own year's average leu rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF), see the GDP entry for detail.
exports.source: Eurostat ext_st_27_2020msbec · exports of goods, world partner, monthly, converted from euros at each month's ECB reference rate (EXR M.RON.EUR.SP00.A).

imports.description: The value of goods Romania buys from the rest of the world each month, in lei.
imports.dollar: Each point is converted at its own year's average leu rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF), see the GDP entry for detail.
imports.source: Eurostat ext_st_27_2020msbec · imports of goods, world partner, monthly, converted from euros at each month's ECB reference rate (EXR M.RON.EUR.SP00.A).

trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods each month. Romania buys more goods from abroad than it sells, every month.
trade_balance.dollar: Each point is converted at its own year's average leu rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF), see the GDP entry for detail.
trade_balance.source: Eurostat ext_st_27_2020msbec · goods trade, world partner, exports minus imports, monthly, not seasonally adjusted, converted from euros at each month's ECB reference rate.

debt_gdp.description: Everything Romania's central government, local government and social security funds owe combined, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
debt_gdp.source: Eurostat gov_10dd_edpt1 · EDP notification table, general government, % of GDP, annual.

deficit.description: The yearly gap between government spending and revenue across all levels of government, as a share of GDP. Negative means a deficit.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
deficit.source: Eurostat gov_10dd_edpt1 · EDP notification table, general government, % of GDP, annual.

fdi.description: Money invested into Romanian businesses from abroad each year (foreign direct investment), as a share of GDP.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
fdi.source: World Bank BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS · % of GDP, annual.

current_account.description: Romania's overall balance with the rest of the world, trade in goods and services plus net investment income, as a share of GDP.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · % of GDP, annual.

fx_usd.description: How many US dollars RON 1 buys. A rising number means a stronger Romanian leu.
fx_usd.source: World Bank series PA.NUS.FCRF · official exchange rate, annual average, shown as US$ per RON 1 (1 ÷ the published RON per US$).

fx_eur.description: How many euros RON 1 buys, on annual averages. A rising number means a stronger Romanian leu.
fx_eur.source: Derived: World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF annual average (RON per US$) and the annual average of Federal Reserve H.10 DEXUSEU; € per RON 1 = (US$ per RON 1) ÷ (US$ per €1).

business_confidence.description: How optimistic firms are about the months ahead. 100 is the long-run average; readings above it mean firms expect better-than-average conditions.
business_confidence.dollar: This is an index, not a currency figure, “Dollarise” doesn't apply to it.
business_confidence.source: OECD · Business Confidence Indicator (BCICP), amplitude-adjusted, long-term average = 100.
